function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
I don’t have direct access to your network, so I can’t measure your speed myself. However, you can easily check it yourself using one of the following methods:

| Method | How to Use |
|--------|------------|
| **Web Speed Test** | Visit a site such as <https://www.speedtest.net> or <https://fast.com>. Click “Go” (or “Start”) and the test will automatically ping a nearby server, download a small file, and report your download/upload speeds and latency. |
| **Command‑Line Tool (speedtest‑cli)** | If you prefer a terminal approach, install the `speedtest-cli` package (`pip install speedtest-cli` on most systems). Then run `speedtest` or `speedtest --simple` to get a quick summary. |
| **Router’s Built‑In Diagnostics** | Many consumer routers include a diagnostics page that runs a speed test against an external server. Check your router’s admin interface (often at 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1) for a “Diagnostics” or “Speed Test” option. |
| **Mobile Apps** | Apps like Ookla’s Speedtest app (available on iOS/Android) perform the same test from your phone or tablet. |

### Quick Tips for Accurate Results
1. **Close other bandwidth‑heavy apps** (streaming, downloads, cloud sync) before testing.  
2. **Use a wired Ethernet connection** if possible; Wi‑Fi can introduce variability.  
3. **Run the test a few times** at different times of day to see typical performance.  

If you’re consistently seeing speeds far below what your ISP advertises, you might want to contact your provider or run a traceroute to identify potential routing issues.
